label: Caesar's wagon rule in Rome
detail: The Law of Caesar on Municipalities bans most wagons from Rome's streets from sunrise to the tenth hour, pushing deliveries into the night.

label: Juvenal can't sleep
detail: Juvenal's third Satire complains that night carts make sleep in Rome impossible for all but the rich.

label: Boston Light first lit
detail: America's oldest light station; a fog cannon followed in 1719.

label: Old North Church's eight bells installed
detail: The treble is inscribed 1744; Paul Revere rang them from 1750 at about age 15.

label: Paul Revere recasts the King's Chapel bell
detail: His largest and last bell.

label: Babbage and Bass's Act
detail: Charles Babbage publishes his Chapter on Street Nuisances; Bass's Act on London street music passes the same year.

label: Boylston and Park Street stations open
detail: Their tight curves cause today's Green Line wheel squeal.

label: Daboll fog trumpet enters service at Graves Light
detail: Replaced a bell buoy a Globe writer called 'weirdly mournful.'

label: Society for the Suppression of Unnecessary Noise
detail: Julia Barnett Rice founds the society in New York, starting with tugboat whistles.

label: Bennett Act
detail: The Bennett Act lets steamboat inspectors regulate whistle use.

label: "Yuyake Koyake" poem written
detail: Uko Nakamura's poem, later set to music, becomes a favorite tune for Japan's 5 p.m. disaster-speaker chime.

label: New York's Noise Abatement Commission
detail: The commission begins measuring New York street noise in decibels.

label: City Noise report
detail: The commission publishes City Noise, a 308-page illustrated report.

label: German siren standard origins
detail: A petitioner told the Bundestag that DIN 14610, the two-tone horn standard, dates from 1935.

label: New York's first noise code
detail: New York City adopts its first comprehensive noise code.

label: Niigata earthquake
detail: Prompts Japan's national bosai musen disaster-speaker system.

label: First FAA aircraft noise standards
detail: FAA sets the first noise standards for new civil subsonic jet designs.

label: The word 'soundscape'
detail: Michael Southworth's 'The sonic environment of cities' is the first scientific use of the word soundscape.

label: Keihan starts a departure melody
detail: One of the early Japanese railway departure melodies.

label: Noise Control Act
detail: The US Noise Control Act directs EPA to regulate product, rail and truck noise; EPA creates ONAC.

label: World Soundscape Project
detail: R. Murray Schafer begins the World Soundscape Project at Simon Fraser University with a study of Vancouver.

label: EPA sets hearing benchmark
detail: US EPA identifies 70 dBA over 24 hours as protective of hearing, and 55 dBA outdoors to avoid annoyance; not a regulation.

label: UK Control of Pollution Act
detail: Gives councils construction-noise powers through section 60 notices and section 61 prior consent.

label: Carmel-by-the-Sea bans leaf blowers
detail: The California town banned leaf blowers as a noise nuisance, among the first US places to do so.

label: "Stage" names introduced
detail: FAA adopts stricter standards and the Stage names; conforming aircraft are called Stage 3.

label: Beverly Hills bans leaf blowers
detail: Beverly Hills, California followed Carmel with its own noise-nuisance ban.

label: Federal truck noise limit
detail: New trucks must emit less than 80 dBA at 50 ft on a drive-by.

label: NRR labels required
detail: EPA requires Noise Reduction Rating labels on US hearing protectors.

label: ONAC defunded
detail: OMB moves to end ONAC's funding and Congress goes along; EPA noise staff fall from 175 to zero, and the office is gone by 1982.

label: Congress defunds EPA's noise office
detail: Congress agrees to cease funding ONAC; EPA stops nearly all noise work and day-to-day control falls to cities.

label: Green Line resilient wheel test
detail: US DOT test finds a light rail vehicle on resilient wheels about 10 dB quieter in-car than a solid-wheel PCC car on the MBTA Green Line.

label: PB/5 crossing button designed
detail: Australian push button with locator chirp, tick-tock and kapow.

label: Massport residential sound insulation program begins
detail: More than 11,000 homes insulated since, FAA-funded.

label: NIOSH measures an ambulance siren
detail: 122 dBA at 10 ft and 98-105 dBA at 100 ft outside the vehicle.

label: Stage 1 big jets banned
detail: Stage 1 aircraft over 75,000 lb phased out of US operation.

label: Motorcycle limit tightens to 80 dBA
detail: EPA noise limit for new street motorcycles drops from 83 dBA (1983) to 80 dBA for model year 1986 and later.

label: JR East melodies at Shinjuku and Shibuya
detail: Departure melodies replace bells at two of Tokyo's busiest stations.

label: MassDEP Noise Policy issued
detail: Sets the 10 dBA-over-ambient and pure tone tests under 310 CMR 7.10.

label: ACUS: repeal or fund
detail: The Administrative Conference of the United States tells Congress to repeal the Noise Control Act or fund it.

label: Heathrow quota count begins
detail: Heathrow starts its points-based night quota system.

label: Sydney Airport Curfew Act
detail: Federal law fixes an 11 pm-6 am curfew at Sydney Airport.

label: UK Pop Code published
detail: The Noise Council publishes its Code of Practice on Environmental Noise Control at Concerts.

label: Car alarms and theft
detail: A Highway Loss Data Institute analysis of 73 million vehicles finds no overall reduction in theft losses for alarm-equipped cars (as cited by Transportation Alternatives).

label: NIOSH backs 3 dB rule
detail: NIOSH criteria recommend 85 dBA with a 3 dB exchange rate.

label: Japan's noise standards take effect
detail: National Environmental Quality Standards for Noise, issued September 30, 1998, set day and night targets by area type.

label: Stage 3 deadline for big jets
detail: Under the Airport Noise and Capacity Act of 1990, US jets over 75,000 lb must meet Stage 3.

label: Big Dig construction noise program published
detail: Erich Thalheimer's paper on the Central Artery/Tunnel noise program; its data later underpinned the FHWA RCNM.

label: EU Environmental Noise Directive
detail: Directive 2002/49/EC is published on 18 July, requiring noise maps and action plans every five years.

label: Great tits sing higher in Leiden
detail: Slabbekoorn and Peet report in Nature that great tits in noisier Leiden territories sing at a higher minimum pitch.

label: Arizona quiet pavement pilot
detail: Arizona DOT starts its Quiet Pavement Pilot Program with FHWA and Volpe.

label: OSHA accepts white-noise backup alarms
detail: A May 27 interpretation letter said reverse alarms need not be single-tone; broadband alarms can comply.

label: Berlin nightingales sing louder
detail: Brumm publishes recordings from 2001-2002 showing nightingales in noisier territories sing louder.

label: FRA train horn rule takes effect
detail: Sets horn levels of 96-110 dB and creates quiet zones.

label: RANCH study
detail: The Lancet publishes RANCH, linking aircraft noise at schools to poorer reading in children.

label: Stage 4 for new designs
detail: Stage 4 (ICAO Chapter 4) applies to new aircraft designs submitted from this date.

label: NYC subway noise survey
detail: Gershon et al. record a 106 dBA platform peak; more than 1 in 10 platform readings above 100 dBA.

label: Urban robins sing at night
detail: Fuller, Warren and Gaston find daytime noise predicts night singing in urban robins better than light does.

label: Rumbler tested by NYPD
detail: Federal Signal's low-frequency siren add-on is tested as an intersection clearing device.

label: New York City's new Noise Code takes effect
detail: Local Law 113 of 2005 replaces the 1972 code with dBA, dBC and octave-band limits and construction mitigation plans.

label: WHO night noise guidelines
detail: WHO Europe sets 40 dB Lnight outside as the night target, with a 55 dB interim target.

label: Windsor Hum reports begin
detail: Residents of Windsor, Ontario began reporting a low hum around this year.

label: Frankfurt night ban
detail: Hesse court bans Frankfurt night flights 23:00-05:00; upheld in Leipzig in April 2012.

label: SAE J1849 stabilized
detail: The US recommended practice for emergency vehicle siren testing.

label: ISO 12913-1 defines soundscape
detail: The ISO standard defines soundscape as the acoustic environment as perceived by people, in context.

label: RNAV procedures concentrate Logan Runway 33L departures
detail: Departures concentrate over north and west Cambridge.

label: Data center arrives in Chandler, Arizona
detail: Residents of Brittany Heights later complained of a nighttime hum after a data center arrived in late 2014.

label: NIOSH tests phone sound apps
detail: Only three apps come within 2 dBA of a reference meter; Android results vary widely by device.

label: Victoria adopts agent of change
detail: Victoria's Live Music Action Agenda puts the onus on the party changing the status quo.

label: Phoenix RNAV routes start
detail: New Sky Harbor departure routes bring more complaints in two weeks than the prior year.

label: 142.2 dBA stadium record
detail: Kansas City Chiefs fans set the Guinness record for loudest stadium crowd roar at Arrowhead Stadium.

label: San Francisco Ordinance 70-15
detail: San Francisco passes an agent-of-change law protecting permitted venues from noise complaints by newer neighbors.

label: London's first Night Czar
detail: Amy Lamé is appointed London's first Night Czar.

label: FAA and Massport launch overflight noise study
detail: MIT helps identify study areas around Logan.

label: First US national noise map
detail: BTS releases the National Transportation Noise Map on March 21, modeling aviation and Interstate noise.

label: CDC Vital Signs on hearing
detail: CDC finds about one in four US adults aged 20 to 69 show signs of noise damage.

label: US National Transportation Noise Map
detail: The Bureau of Transportation Statistics releases its first national map of aviation and Interstate noise.

label: Boylston curve in the news
detail: WBUR reports the MBTA has 13 greaser units on the Green Line and is testing graphite flange-stick lubricators.

label: France caps concert sound
detail: Decree 2017-1244 caps amplified sound at 102 dB(A) and 118 dB(C), each over 15 minutes.

label: Phoenix wins in court
detail: D.C. Circuit vacates the FAA's Phoenix route approval as arbitrary and capricious.

label: WHO Environmental Noise Guidelines
detail: WHO Europe publishes source-specific guidelines; aircraft gets the strictest values (45 dB Lden, 40 dB Lnight).

label: England adds agent of change to planning policy
detail: The revised National Planning Policy Framework includes the agent of change principle.

label: BU Community Noise Lab launches
detail: Introduces the NoiseScore app.

label: WHO-ITU H.870
detail: Voluntary safe listening standard for personal audio devices.

label: Toronto's new noise bylaw in force
detail: Chapter 591 sets amplified-sound limits in both dBA and dBC at the point of reception.

label: Zug Island scaled back; Windsor Hum fades
detail: U.S. Steel scaled back Zug Island from April 1; by July a lead researcher said he had not heard the hum for almost a year.

label: Lockdown quiets the planet
detail: Seismometers record up to 50% less high-frequency ground noise during COVID-19 lockdowns.

label: Mumbai punishing signal
detail: Decibel meters reset the red light when honking tops 85 dB.

label: Maryland case dismissed
detail: D.C. Circuit dismisses Maryland's DCA flight path challenge as untimely.

label: FMVSS 141 full compliance
detail: All new US hybrids and EVs must make a warning sound at low speed.

label: Curved RNP approach to Logan Runway 33L implemented
detail: Same year, most CAC communities vote against an MIT 33L departure proposal.

label: California passes AB 1346
detail: The law halts sale of most new small off-road gas engines, including blowers and mowers, by 2024.

label: Final Windsor Hum report released
detail: The July report named Zug Island's blast furnaces as the likely source.

label: FAA survey results released
detail: Neighborhood Environmental Survey shows 60-71% highly annoyed at DNL 65.

label: NYC noise camera pilot
detail: NYC DEP begins piloting noise cameras triggered at 85 decibels from at least 50 feet.

label: EU AVAS on all new EVs
detail: Acoustic warning systems required on all new electric and hybrid vehicles in the EU.

label: California AB 1346
detail: Phases out sales of most new small gas engines, including leaf blowers, from 2024.

label: WHO venue standard
detail: WHO global standard for safe listening venues caps levels at 100 dB LAeq over 15 minutes.

label: Misophonia consensus
detail: An expert panel publishes the first consensus definition of misophonia.

label: Global tinnitus estimate
detail: JAMA Neurology meta-analysis puts adult tinnitus prevalence at 14.4%.

label: Washington, DC gas blower ban takes effect
detail: The District's ban on gas-powered leaf blowers took effect January 1.

label: Washington, DC gas leaf blower ban
detail: The District's 2018 law barring gas-powered leaf blowers takes effect.

label: France noise radar trial
detail: Legal trial of the Hydre noise radar begins under the 2019 mobility law.

label: WHO safe listening standard
detail: WHO releases its voluntary Global standard for safe listening venues and events, with a 100 dB LAeq,15min limit.

label: California SB 1079 signed
detail: Requires the CHP to evaluate sound-activated enforcement devices.

label: UK noise camera trial starts
detail: DfT roadside trial in four areas, funded at 300,000 pounds.

label: Chandler data center noise ordinance
detail: Per the Prince William Times, a January ordinance required a noise liaison and a pre-construction baseline.

label: Boston names a nightlife director
detail: Corean Reynolds becomes Boston's first Director of Nightlife Economy.

label: Minneapolis allows all five calls to prayer
detail: Minneapolis removes time limits that blocked amplified dawn and late-evening calls to prayer.

label: Noise Policy Review opens
detail: FAA asks for comment on DNL and the 65 DNL threshold; 4,857 comments received.

label: Stop Spreading the Noise Act
detail: NYC Council allows noise cameras in all five boroughs.

label: Virginia JLARC data center review
detail: Found nearly one-third of Virginia data centers within 200 feet of residentially zoned property.

label: Cicada dual brood
detail: Broods XIII and XIX emerge together for the first time in 221 years.

label: Toronto lowers night limits
detail: Council cuts indoor night amplified-sound limits to 42 dBA and 57 dBC and allows property-line measurement.

label: Germany closes wail-and-yelp petition
detail: Yelp allowed only as a police and customs stop signal; the two-tone horn stays the only warning tone.

label: UK trial reports published
detail: 1,777 activations, 4% attributed to excessively noisy vehicles.

label: Cambridge, Massachusetts bans gas blowers
detail: Boston's neighbor banned gas leaf blowers, according to Wikipedia.

label: CHP noise camera report
detail: CHP does not recommend the devices as a standalone basis for citations.

label: JR East to phase out local melodies
detail: Platform melodies to give way to standard melodies played from trains.

label: NYC helicopter bill passes
detail: City Council passes Intro 26-A limiting non-essential flights at two Manhattan heliports from 2029.

label: EEA noise report
detail: EEA estimates 73,000 premature deaths a year in Europe from transport noise.

label: MassDEP proposes noise policy revisions
detail: Including a 40 dBA presumption of acceptability; comments closed April 30, 2026.

label: Court rules EPA neglected the Noise Control Act
detail: A federal judge finds EPA unlawfully neglected its duties under the 1972 Act; remedies are left to later proceedings.

label: Supersonic overland rule proposed
detail: FAA proposes allowing overland supersonic flight with surface booms at or below 0.11 psf.

label: Boston City Council files noise enforcement hearing order
detail: Nine councilors ask for complaint, response-time and citation data; a resolution followed July 24.
